# Report information

Focused **protein-level** report for immunopeptidomics experiments. Every other
report describes peptides; this one condenses them to their **source proteins** —
which proteins the presented ligands came from, how many each contributed, how
widely each is detected, and what the search engine itself reported about them.
It is deliberately descriptive: the caveats that make protein-level
immunopeptidomics easy to over-read are documented in the *Methods & caveats*
section at the end.

`r HowMaHiCo::provider_line(params$Provider)`

**Sample Set:** `r params$SampleSet`

**Data Analysis: ** `r params$DataAnalysisNames`

**Date:**  `r Sys.Date()`

**Code version:** `r packageVersion("HowMaHiCo")`

```{r child = system.file("rmarkdown", "shared", "setup.Rmd", package = "HowMaHiCo")}
```


```{r prot-all-prep, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=TRUE}
# ---- inputs -----------------------------------------------------------------
prot_input <- if (params$PeptideSet == "all") pep_all else pep_short
peptide_set_label <- if (params$PeptideSet == "all") "all peptides" else
  paste0("selected peptides (", shortpep_range[1], " to ", shortpep_range[2], " AAs)")

# ---- the protein table ------------------------------------------------------
prot_all <- build_prot_all(prot_input,
                           protein = params$ProteinFeature,
                           multi_mapping = params$MultiMapping)
prot_summary <- summarise_prot_all(prot_all, by = "Condition")
top_proteins <- top_source_proteins(prot_all, n = params$TopNProteins,
                                    min_peptides = params$MinPeptidesProtein)
top_proteins_area <- top_source_proteins(prot_all, n = params$TopNProteins,
                                         by = "Area",
                                         min_peptides = params$MinPeptidesProtein)

n_proteins <- dplyr::n_distinct(prot_all$Protein)
n_accessions <- dplyr::n_distinct(prot_input$Accession)

# ---- what the search engine reported at protein level -----------------------
engine_cols <- prot_engine_columns(prot_input)
engine_quant <- c(engine_cols$quantity, engine_cols$qvalue)
has_engine_quant <- length(engine_quant) > 0 &&
  any(vapply(engine_quant, function(nm) any(!is.na(prot_all[[nm]])), logical(1)))

varied <- attr(prot_all, "engine_columns_varied")
if (!is.null(varied) && length(varied) > 0)
  warning("Engine-reported value(s) varied within a ", params$ProteinFeature,
          " group and were set to NA rather than averaged: ",
          paste(names(varied), varied, sep = " (", collapse = " groups), "), " groups).")
```

**Peptide set:** `r peptide_set_label` &nbsp;|&nbsp; **protein key:**
`r params$ProteinFeature` &nbsp;|&nbsp; **multi-mapping:** `r params$MultiMapping`
&nbsp;|&nbsp; **source proteins:** `r format(n_proteins, big.mark = ",")`

# Source proteins

Each row of the exported `prot_all` table is one (protein, sample) pair: how many
ligands that protein contributed to that sample, their summed intensity, and the
protein's annotation.

> **This count and the one in `01_id_counts` need not agree.** The identification
> reports count proteins as distinct `Accession` values
> (`r format(n_accessions, big.mark = ",")` here); this report groups on
> **`r params$ProteinFeature`** (`r format(n_proteins, big.mark = ",")` here). For
> FragPipe the two coincide; for DIA-NN, where `Accession` holds a `;`-separated
> list of every mapped protein, they do not. Neither is wrong — they answer
> different questions.

```{r plot-proteins-per-sample, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, warning=FALSE}
p_proteins_per_sample <- plot_proteins_per_sample(prot_all)
if (is.null(p_proteins_per_sample))
  cat("_No source protein could be assigned in this subset._") else
  ggprint_rawr(p_proteins_per_sample)
```

```{r proteins-per-condition-table, echo=FALSE}
prot_all |>
  dplyr::group_by(Condition) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n_Proteins = dplyr::n_distinct(Protein),
                   n_Peptides = sum(n_Peptides, na.rm = TRUE),
                   Peptides_per_protein = round(n_Peptides / n_Proteins, 2),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(caption = "Source proteins per Condition") |>
  kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE)
```

## Table

```{r top-proteins-table, echo=FALSE}
if (nrow(top_proteins) == 0) {
  cat("_No protein passed MinPeptidesProtein._")
} else {
  top_proteins |>
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric),
                                function(x) signif(x, 4))) |>
    DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
                  options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE))
}
```

# Protein-level intensity

Summed ligand `Area` per source protein: the intensities of all its peptides
added on the linear scale within each sample. Read it as "how much signal did
this protein's ligands carry", **not** as the protein's abundance — see
*Methods & caveats*.

```{r plot-top-proteins-area, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=7, warning=FALSE}
p_top_proteins_area <- plot_top_proteins(top_proteins_area, by = "Area")
if (is.null(p_top_proteins_area))
  cat("_No usable `Area` in this subset._") else
  ggprint_rawr(p_top_proteins_area)
```

```{r prot-summary-table, echo=FALSE}
prot_summary |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n_Peptides_total)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric),
                              function(x) signif(x, 4))) |>
  DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
                caption = "Per-protein summary by Condition",
                options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE))
```

```{r engine-quant-section, echo=FALSE, results='asis', fig.width=8, fig.height=6, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
p_ligand_vs_quant <- NULL

if (!has_engine_quant) {
  cat("\n# Search-engine protein data\n\n")
  cat("_The search engine behind this dataset (**",
      paste(unique(stats::na.omit(as.character(prot_input$Found_By))), collapse = ", "),
      "**) reports no protein-level values, so this section is empty. ",
      "DIA-NN reports protein-group quantities (`PG.MaxLFQ` and relatives) and ",
      "q-values, which are carried through automatically when present. ",
      "FragPipe's protein quantities live in `protein.tsv`, which this package ",
      "does not read._\n\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("\n# Search-engine protein data\n\n")
  cat("Values computed by the search engine itself and carried through unchanged.",
      "They are scoped to the search engine's own protein groups, so they are",
      "reported per (protein, sample) exactly as found; where a value differed",
      "within a group it is `NA` rather than an average.\n\n")

  cat("\n## Reported values\n\n")
  # kable, not DT: an htmlwidget printed from inside a results='asis' chunk needs
  # an explicit tagList/knit_print dance to have its dependencies attached, and
  # silently renders empty when that is missed.
  keep <- c("Protein", "Sample", "Condition", "n_Peptides", "Area", engine_quant)
  tbl <- prot_all[, intersect(keep, names(prot_all)), drop = FALSE]
  tbl <- tbl |>
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric), function(x) signif(x, 4)))
  print(kable_paper(kable(utils::head(tbl, 50),
                          caption = paste0("Engine-reported protein values (first 50 of ",
                                           nrow(tbl), " rows; the full table is in ",
                                           "prot_all.csv)")),
                    "hover", full_width = FALSE))

  cat("\n\n## Ligand intensity vs. the engine's protein quantity\n\n")
  p_ligand_vs_quant <- plot_ligand_vs_protein_quant(prot_all)
  if (is.null(p_ligand_vs_quant)) {
    cat("_No protein has both a summed ligand Area and an engine quantity._\n\n")
  } else {
    print(p_ligand_vs_quant)
    cat("\n\nA weak correlation is the expected result, not a problem: HLA",
        "presentation is shaped by processing and binding, so ligand intensity",
        "and source-protein abundance measure different things.\n\n")
  }
}
```

# Methods & caveats

**What the table is.** One row per (protein, `Sample`). Peptides are grouped by
**`r params$ProteinFeature`**; `Area` is summed on the linear scale within a
sample and log2-transformed afterwards, matching `build_quant_matrix()`. Note
that the protein matrices in `00_mhc_report`/`04_quant` take a different route —
`get_mat_log2area()` *averages* `Log2Area` — so those numbers are not comparable
with these.

**Summed ligand intensity is not protein abundance.** How much of a protein is
presented depends on proteasomal processing, peptide transport and HLA binding
affinity, not only on how much protein is there. Where the search engine reports
a real protein quantity, both are shown side by side rather than one standing in
for the other.

**Engine-reported values are the search engine's.** `PG.MaxLFQ` and its relatives
are computed by DIA-NN from the same precursors under its own normalisation and
protein-group inference. They are carried through unchanged, and are not
comparable across a re-search with different settings.

**No length normalisation.** Longer proteins yield more ligands simply by being
longer, so the ranking above is partly a protein-length ranking. The metric that
actually identifies *over-presented* proteins is ligands per unit length, which
needs the search FASTA — out of scope for this report.

**Protein inference is weak for short, non-tryptic peptides.** An 8–11-mer often
maps to several proteins, and `MultiMapping` picks between two imperfect
conventions. This run used **`r params$MultiMapping`**:
`r if (params$MultiMapping == "leading") "each peptide was counted once, for its leading protein, so per-protein ligand counts still sum to the number of peptides — at the cost of attributing shared ligands somewhat arbitrarily." else "each peptide was counted for every protein it maps to, so no candidate is discarded — but per-protein ligand counts deliberately exceed the number of peptides in the dataset, and promiscuous regions inflate their proteins."`

**Protein counts differ between reports.** See the note in *Source proteins*:
`01_id_counts` counts distinct `Accession` values, this report groups on
`r params$ProteinFeature`.

**Decoys and contaminants are carried through** unless they were filtered
upstream. `check_ids_global()`, shown in `01_id_counts`, is the view of that
split.

```{r export-results, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Always-written exports: render parameters + the protein table and its summary
write_input_params(params, folder = FolderResults,
                   prefix = paste(c(result_prefix, "08_prot_all"), collapse = "_"))
write.csv_rawr(prot_all, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)
write.csv_rawr(prot_summary, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)

if (params$CsvSave) {
  prot_top_proteins <- top_proteins
  prot_top_proteins_area <- top_proteins_area
  write.csv_rawr(prot_top_proteins, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)
  write.csv_rawr(prot_top_proteins_area, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)
}

if (params$PlotsSave) {
  static_plots <- list(p_proteins_per_sample = p_proteins_per_sample,
                       p_peptides_per_protein = p_peptides_per_protein,
                       p_peptides_per_protein_violin = p_peptides_per_protein_violin,
                       p_top_proteins = p_top_proteins,
                       p_top_proteins_area = p_top_proteins_area,
                       p_protein_detection_sample = p_protein_detection_sample,
                       p_protein_detection_condition = p_protein_detection_condition,
                       p_ligand_vs_quant = p_ligand_vs_quant)
  for (nm in names(static_plots)) {
    if (!is.null(static_plots[[nm]]))
      ggsave_rawr(static_plots[[nm]], file = nm, folder = FolderFigures,
                  width = 20, height = 14)
  }
}
```
